title: terraform: unify private state layout for GPU node pools, IAM, and networking
author: Aisha Raman
description:
Motivation: private deployments currently have fragmented Terraform state layouts for GPU node pools, IAM roles/policies, and networking resources. This makes cross-resource refactors and upgrades error-prone during private installer upgrades and when migrating customer state backends. This PR unifies the state layout and updates modules to support a single, extensible backend layout for VPC/on-prem/private deployments.

What this PR does: - Moves per-cluster GPU node pool state into a shared "private_clusters/{cluster_name}" namespace while keeping historical resource IDs stable via migration scripts. - Extracts IAM role and policy resources into a dedicated module with stable resource addresses and explicit outputs for the private control plane. - Reworks networking modules (subnets, route tables, VPN attachments) to emit metadata required by the private installer and Helm charts. - Adds a state migration helper and documented tfstate migration plan for customers (linear links and notes). - Adds unit/integration test fixtures for GCP/AWS backends and updates CI to run terraform validate/plan against the new layout.

Checklist: - [x] Module refactor for gpu_node_pool (preserve resource addresses where possible) - [x] New module redwood_private_iam with clear outputs - [x] Networking module updates and outputs for installer - [x] Migration helper scripts and docs - [x] CI plan/validate updates - [x] Reviewed and approved by infra team

Notes: The migration scripts included are additive and can be run by operators prior to a major upgrade. We do not automatically migrate customer state; instead we provide a safe, documented path and a rollback plan. See release_notes for a short summary to include in the private-deploy upgrade docs.

ci_logs_summary: Initial CI run: terraform validate failed on networking module (missing output). Fix applied and re-run. Second run: all validate/plan checks passed. Integration fixture plan for AWS showed no resource replacements once migration script applied to fixture state.
release_notes:
- Unify Terraform state layout for private deployments (GPU node pools, IAM, networking)
- Add migration helper scripts and documented migration plan for operators
- CI updates: validate/plan gates for private module changes
Operator action: run provided migration helper before upgrading private installer to the next major release.
testing_notes: Local: ran terraform validate/plan for AWS and GCP fixtures. Applied migration helper to fixture states and ran plan to assert no destructive changes. CI: validate and plan gates added; artifacts stored for manual inspection.
upgrade_impact: This is an additive refactor but requires operators to run state migration helper prior to upgrading. We've included a rollback plan in examples/private-deploy/migration-plan.md.
customer_implications: Customers on earlier private versions will need to coordinate a short maintenance window to run the migration helper. No automatic state changes will be performed by the installer.
notes_for_release: Document in private-deploy upgrade playbook and notify SRE/customer success for scheduled migrations.
security_considerations: IAM module changes preserve least-privilege roles; outputs only expose ARNs/IDs required by the installer. Migration scripts read state but do not store secrets. We ran an internal scan for leaked outputs.
support_notes: Support runbook added at docs/upgrade/private-state-migration.md. Escalation path: ENG-7345.
changelog_entry: Unify private Terraform state layout and add migration helpers (operators must run migration helper before upgrade).
